summary: Maximise profit from one buy followed by one sell (0 if no profit is possible).
mainInsight: Scan once while tracking the lowest price seen so far (the best buy day up to now); selling today yields price - min_price, so keep the maximum of that over all days.
canonicalApproach: Single pass with a running minimum

approaches.name: Single pass with a running minimum
approaches.summary: min_buy = min(min_buy, p); best = max(best, p - min_buy).

cards.answer: Single pass tracking the lowest price so far and the best profit. Clue: You buy once and sell on a later day, so for each day the best buy is the cheapest earlier price, which one pass can remember; with up to 10^5 days checking all pairs is too slow.
keyPoints: You buy once and sell on a later day, so for each day the best buy is the cheapest earlier price, which one pass can remember; with up to 10^5 days checking all pairs is too slow.
cards.explanation: Profit on a given day depends only on the minimum price seen before it, so a running minimum and a running maximum profit are enough.

promptVariants: Why is one pass with a running minimum enough?
How does this relate to Kadane's algorithm?
cards.answer: Profit for selling on day i is price[i] - min(price[0..i-1]); the minimum prefix is easy to maintain. Equivalently it is the maximum subarray of daily differences (Kadane) - both are O(n) single-pass DP over prefixes.
cards.explanation: You cannot sell before you buy, which the prefix minimum enforces.

promptVariants: Why update min_buy before computing the profit in the same iteration?
What is the profit on a falling price series?
cards.code:
min_buy = prices[0]
max_profit = 0
for i in range(len(prices)):
    min_buy = min(min_buy, prices[i])
    max_profit = max(max_profit, prices[i] - min_buy)
cards.answer: If today is the new minimum then prices[i] - min_buy = 0, which is harmless (buy and sell on the same day gives zero profit). The order guarantees min_buy is never greater than today's price. For a strictly falling series every profit is 0, so the answer is 0 (max_profit starts at 0).
keyPoints: Update min first: profit 0 at a new low
cards.explanation: Starting the loop at index 1 would be equivalent.
Falling prices give no profit (0). In [3,8,1,6] buying at 3 and selling at 8 gives 5, which beats 1 -> 6 (also 5).

incorrectOptionExplanations.-7, and 5: Profit is never negative: you may simply not trade.
incorrectOptionExplanations.0, and 7: 8 - 1 = 7 sells before it buys; the buy must come first.
incorrectOptionExplanations.2, and 5: Prices only fall in the first array, so there is no profit.
